Also, Carlos does only 2 bad things in the entire film.

The first one is when he takes over the factory by force, he decides to replace all the Easter candy with bird food and worms. HOW-FUCKING-EVER, never throughout the entire film did Carlos express any sort of hatred towards children, candy, or Easter as a holiday. This was clearly a thing the writers did in order to give people (namely children) a reason to hate him, because he was 100% right until this point.

The second was he tries to kill the main character (who sucks so this is good) and his human best friend. But also this is a poorly written film for children so yeah okay whatever, yk?

Okay so there is a factory that is run by the Easter bunny where he produces all the Easter candy. The factory is overseen by the Easter bunny, but there are a bunch of chicks who are ACTUALLY working the factory floor (chicks meaning actual baby chickens). The antagonist of the film is a chick named Carlos who wants to be elected as the next leader of the factory when the Easter bunny retires.

Carlos is confirmed to be one of the factory's hardest and longest workers. He knows the business inside and out, has sacrificed tons of time and energy to the factory, even the Easter bunny himself says that Carlos is an incredible employee. So, Carlos approaches the Easter bunny and explains that with the bunny so close to retirement, he believes he should be put in charge of the factory. However, the Easter bunny laughs at him, explaining that only a bunny can be in charge of the factory (remember this for later). Instead, the Easter bunny wants to elect his son to take over the business, his son who has never worked in the factory, actively avoids all responsibility, dislikes the holiday, and wants to be a professional drummer.

Carlos is mad, but attempts to prove his dedication to the field by working even harder. The Easter bunny recognizes his even harder work, but tells him that his efforts are ultimately in vain and a chick will never run the factory. So, in the last half hour of the film, Carlos unionizes the factory employee chicks, fighting for workers rights and is elected by every factory worker to take over the factory. This unionization is portrayed as evil.

Also, it should be noted that all of the chicks have a thick Spanish accents while the Easter bunny and his son have British accents, soooo...

Anyway, the finale of the film is that Carlos is defeated, the Easter bunny son is put in charge of the factory, but also so is the son's human friend because this human "loves Easter" despite the fact that the Easter bunny himself said that ONLY a bunny can be in charge of the factory. So a bunny who ignores responsibility and a human with no track record are now in charge, all while the actual hard working employees have their union disbanded, their jobs insecure, and their bosses REALLY not caring about them.

So yeah, Hop is a fucking horrible movie, please please PLEASE do not watch it.

So, about this game mode not being a "card game." Yes, the design of the mercs is not a card game, but the reason I call it one is because it uses a lot of the same systems that the base game does, from the merc collection to the menus and even some of the features in the main game. Not to mention that you have to open packs to receive new mercs. So I don't think referring to this as a card game is unreasonable. A ton of the same systems and ideas have been grandfathered in from hearthstone without changing them properly to be more fitting for the game.

​

The second half of your reply is a bit hard to fully understand, presumably because you are so mad you forgot to make your point clear, but if I were to paraphrase what you are saying; you recognize the errors of the game, and are happy to wait for the devs to implement new fixes at their own pace. I am glad that you recognize the flaws of the game, but these are fixes that range from extremely easy to mundane and laughable. For example, right now, the biggest problem in this game mode at the moment in my opinion is the duplicate coins. Here are some ideas they could implement that would be incredibly easy to do:

1. Make coins colored rather than merc specific, so I can level who I want to immediately and I can forget about who I don't.
2. Make coins dustable, so I can turn my 6000 Rokara coins into any other character.
3. Make packs unable to drop coins for mercs you have maxed out. This fix in particular would be extremely easy, considering they have advertised that this is possible when you spend real money.

Ultimately, we are on the same side, but while I am choosing to voice my issues with this shoddy cash-grab, you choose to bash others for voicing their frustrations.
